dict.string: Open a pasted file path, folder path, or URL with macOS. Show an alert when it cannot be opened.

input="$1"
# Finder's Copy as Pathname may wrap paths containing spaces in quotes. case "$input" in \'*\') input=${input#\'}; input=${input%\'} ;; \"*\") input=${input#\"}; input=${input%\"} ;; esac
# Make the common ~/path notation work even though it arrives as an argument. case "$input" in '~') input="$HOME" ;; '~/'*) input="$HOME/${input#~/}" ;; esac
alert() { /usr/bin/osascript -e 'on run argv' -e 'display alert "Open Path" message (item 1 of argv) as critical' -e 'end run' "$1" }
if [ -z "$input" ]; then alert 'Please enter a path or URL.' exit 0 fi
case "$input" in *://*|mailto:*|tel:*) ;; *) if [ ! -e "$input" ]; then alert "Path does not exist: $input" exit 0 fi ;; esac
case "$input" in *://*|mailto:*|tel:*) open "$input" || alert "Could not open: $input" ;; *) if [ -d "$input" ]; then open "$input" || alert "Could not open: $input" else # Reveal files in Finder without opening their associated application. open -R "$input" || alert "Could not reveal: $input" fi ;; esac

Usage: invoke Alfred, type go followed by a space and a file path, folder path, or URL, then press Return once. Folders and URLs open immediately; files are revealed and selected in Finder; invalid paths show an alert.
